描述_EN: near the edges are huge guardian figures, chinese on the left and foreign on the right. above, musicians accompany the deceased on his journey to the afterlife. sogdians, natives of modern uzbekistan, travelled and traded in north china. they practised zoroastrianism, a fire-worshipping religion, and exposed their dead rather than cremating them. in the centre of the panel is a zoroastrian fire altar, flanked by half-human attendants. this slab supported a rectangular coffin platform, or funerary couch, made for a sogdian official.
描述_ZN: 靠近边缘的是巨大的守护者形象，左边是中国人，右边是外国人。 上面，音乐家们在死者的来世之旅中陪伴他。 索格达人，现代乌兹别克斯坦的土著，在中国北方旅行和贸易。 他们信奉拜火教，是一种火崇拜的宗教，他们将死者暴露在外面，而不是火化他们。 在画板的中央是一个拜火教的祭坛，两侧是半人的侍者。 这块板子支撑着一个长方形的棺材平台，或者说是殡仪馆的沙发，是为一个索格底亚官员制作的。
